_how: The crew as data. One entry per division, one per worker. Adding a worker is adding an entry here: 'impl' names its implementation in workers.IMPLS, 'provider' names an entry in 'providers' (the minimum seconds between two requests to that host, shared by every worker on it). Worker ids are '<division>.<name>' and must be unique; an unknown field, impl, provider or division is an error at load time. Moss is not in this file: she is a separate process (C:\src\Galatea) that reads the leaders' reports and sets each division's goal and compute share.

divisions.title: Posting
divisions.leader_notes: Two workers post: posting.blog (blog posts on the website) and posting.instagram (Instagram card posts). Each row names its worker; report the two separately. Each worker's post.tally holds its counts: drafts written, drafts blocked, posts submitted for approval, posts pending approval, posts published, posts denied. A post PENDING APPROVAL has NOT been published: say it is waiting for the owner's approval, never that it is out. Only a post.published row is a published post; give its URL for the blog, its permalink for Instagram. A post.blocked row is a draft the content check stopped before anyone saw it: say so and give its reasons by kind (a name not on the allowlist, a link or domain, personal data, a business number, an internal system name, text that does not fit the Instagram card) without repeating any name the reasons quote. A post.not_published row says why a submitted post did not go out (denied by the owner, failed, or done without a URL or permalink).
